newsitem.title: USA: US junk bond funds get $313 mln in new cash-AMG.
newsitem.headline: US junk bond funds get $313 mln in new cash-AMG.

text.p: U.S. high-yield bond mutual funds received net cash inflows of $313 million in the latest recorded week which ended July 16, according to AMG Data Services.
This week's number represented the seventh consecutive week of positive net cash flows from mutual funds into the junk bond market.
Since the beginning of June, approximately $2.3 billion in new cash has poured into junk bond mutual funds, according to AMG.
In the prior two weeks, inflows totalled $389 million and $182.1 million, respectively, AMG reported.
The information is tallied from high-yield bond funds that report on a weekly basis. AMG excludes reinvested distributions, therefore representing only net new money coming into funds.
Mutual fund cash flows are closely watched by junk bond players because the high-yield bond market has one of the heaviest concentrations of mutual fund money of any major asset class in the U.S.
Analysts estimate 25-40 percent of all outstanding junk bonds are held by mutual funds.
AMG, based in Arcata, Calif., compiles information on U.S. mutual funds.
